Subject: Clarification: KEK rollover with zero-downtime + TLS binding specifics

Hi Irene,

Thanks for the initial answers in the RFP packet — a few follow-ups from our security team:

- We also require the TLS binding details for tenant-level endpoints when BYOK is enabled: which cipher suites you support, whether mTLS is enforced per-tenant, and how you bind tenant certificates to the KEK lifecycle.
- Finally, can you provide a copy of your HSM attestation chain and any evidence of remote key import controls?

Can you get these to us by next Monday (16 Nov)? MedSolve needs the artifacts for our internal risk committee.

Subject: Re: Clarification: KEK rollover with zero-downtime + TLS binding specifics

Hi Alex — thanks for the clear list. We're prepping a short runbook and the TLS binding matrix; attaching the initial versions for review. High-level answers here, full artifacts attached:  

- Zero-downtime KEK rollover: Redwood supports in-place KEK rotation using HSM-backed KEKs and envelope encryption. We stagger rewrapping at object/tenant granularity and use background rewrap workers with priority-aware batching to avoid service interruptions. In our tests with comparable workloads we observe no measurable increase to 99th percentile latency; transient CPU/IO load can increase tokenization/IO times for a small set of long-lived streams (we call these "rekey waves"). We include automatic rate-limiting of rewrap workers and a fallback path that serves from the previous KEK for any in-flight sessions.

- TLS binding for BYOK: When a tenant enables BYOK we map their certificate chain to a tenant key handle; the KEK lifecycle governs the wrapped tenant key material. We support per-tenant mTLS enforcement as an opt-in configuration (recommended for high-privilege workloads). Attached is a cipher-suite matrix with recommended defaults; for MedSolve we suggest TLS1.3 with AES-GCM or CHACHA20_POLY1305 and ECDHE key exchange.

- HSM attestation and import controls: Attached is the HSM attestation chain (PEM) and a short summary of our remote key import policy — all imports require dual-operator approval, hardware-backed attestations, and are audited in our immutable ledger.

Deliverables attached: redwood_zero-downtime-kek-rollout_plan_v1.pdf, tls_cipher_binding_matrix.xlsx, hsm_attestation_chain.pem

We can walk through the runbook on a quick call if helpful — propose Wed 11/11 or Fri 11/13.

Best,
Irene Choi
Director, Product Security — Redwood Inference

Looping in a couple of technical clarifications for the artifacts before we send them to MedSolve:  
1) Runbook: add an explicit subsection on the "rekey wave" detection thresholds and the exact automatic throttling parameters we use (max concurrent rewrap threads per GPU node, backoff window). MedSolve will ask for numbers.
2) Cipher matrix: include client-negotiation examples (server pref vs client pref) and the explicit ciphers we will disallow for compliance (e.g., AES-CBC, RC4).
3) Attestation: confirm the chain includes the vendor firmware hash for the HSM and note the validity window for the attestation. Also add the KMIP proxy controls for on-prem key import requests.

I'll draft the additions — @Kimberly, can you compile the firmware hash snippet + the KMIP proxy text? Priyom, please verify the throttling numbers from the runtime team (we used 8 threads/node in the lab).

Rishi

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Porter <alex.porter@medsolve.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, MedSolve Procurement <procurement@medsolve.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Nov 2026 14:40:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Clarification: KEK rollover with zero-downtime + TLS binding specifics

Alex — thanks for your patience. Per Rishi's notes we've updated the artifacts and are happy to share a concise appendix here:  

- Rekey wave thresholds and throttling: default detection is when >0.5% of tenant objects are queued for rewrap within a 3-minute window. Defaults: 8 rewrap threads per GPU node, max global rewrap concurrency 256, exponential backoff starting at 250ms with 2x factor up to 4s. During production runbooks these values are tuned per-customer workload (we documented MedSolve recommended starting values in the runbook).

- Expected impact: for mixed-read/write workloads we observed a 0–5% increase in CPU usage for a 30–90 minute maintenance window and no change to 99th percentile request latency in our benchmark (we include the test harness results in the runbook appendix).

- TLS/cipher binding: server-preferred negotiation only. We explicitly disable AES-CBC, RC4, and all RSA key-exchange ciphers. For BYOK + tenant mTLS we bind the tenant certificate Subject/Serial to the tenant key handle and the KEK wrap metadata contains the KEK version used at the time of wrap (so you can reconstruct which KEK protected which wrapped-key).

- HSM attestation: attached PEM includes vendor chain and firmware hash + attestation timestamp window (valid for 30 days from issuance). KMIP proxy notes added: on-prem imports require an HSM-wrapped blob plus remote attestation and a signed import request; only dual-operator can approve.

Attachments: redwood_zero-downtime-kek-rollout_plan_v1.pdf (updated appendix), tls_cipher_binding_matrix.xlsx (updated), hsm_attestation_chain.pem (full chain + firmware metadata)

Next steps: if MedSolve's committee needs a short 30-minute walkthrough we can schedule Thu 11/18 10am ET. Otherwise, happy to incorporate any final clarifications in a follow-up.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Sr. Manager, Product Security Programs — Redwood Inference
